examine: The records closet is alphabetized by motive, moon phase, and snack preference.
Opening it without a warrant would release at least three decades of dust.
The secure hotline only calls payphones that have not been invented yet.
Someone left a message: 'Bring the polymorphic dongle. And snacks.'
A suitcase cyberdeck with a phosphor display and three keyboards. None agree on where Escape is.
Its packet-origami chip allegedly folds a hypothetical network until two distant ports touch.
The cabinet contains forbidden silicon: moon-phase timers and one chip labeled DO NOT LICK.
Perfect for imaginary capers involving air-gapped vending machines.
A spectral signal diviner. It finds ghost packets by listening for tiny apologies after missed handshakes.
The brass dial selects NORMAL, ESOTERIC, or PLAUSIBLE DENIABILITY.

talk: I traced the signal through three dead relays. Someone wants us to find the source.
Check the junkyard. And try not to antagonize anything with more antennas than sense.

examine: A once-proud getaway car, retired after its dashboard developed root access and locked the driver out.
The glove box still contains a hypothetical CAN-bus séance kit. It asks the engine control unit questions through interpretive blinking.
The trashcan is full of shredded one-time pads, expired access badges, and a banana peel with suspiciously good opsec.
At the bottom: an esoteric refuse-collection chip that exfiltrates nothing except the smell. A flawless threat model.
